meta_title: Not a Zoho Inventory Alternative: Keep It, Add Voice Ordering
meta_desc: Keep Zoho Inventory for stock, price lists and its portal. Restaurants that call speak orders into an app and check each item. Not a Zoho Inventory alternative.

hero.h1: Not A Zoho Inventory Alternative: Orders Without The Call
hero.lead: Zoho's customer portal lets a restaurant pay a bill, but not start an order. Inside the VoiceOrder Solutions app, your customer's chef talks through what is short and reviews each item before it reaches you. Zoho Inventory carries on with your stock, prices and portal.

problem.h2: Why some distributors search for a Zoho Inventory competitor
problem.lead: If you are weighing a Zoho Inventory alternative, look first at what a restaurant can do once it logs in to Zoho's portal: it can view its orders and pay its bills there, but has nowhere to put the next one, so that order still reaches you by phone. An order the app emails you is still keyed in by your team, though the chef checked every item before it was sent. Through EDI or the API it can go into Zoho directly if your account allows it, and we check that in the demo.

cards.h3: Kitchens pay in the portal, then call to order
cards.body: Zoho's help pages say it plainly: customers "cannot add items and place orders directly from the customer portal." They can view sales orders, pay invoices and check deliveries there. Tomorrow's order still arrives as a call, a text or a voicemail.

cards.h3: Calls turn into typing for your team
cards.body: In Zoho Inventory, your team creates the sales orders for anything phoned in, at a desk or in its mobile app. A chef's 6 a.m. call only becomes an order in Zoho once somebody has time to key it in.

cards.h3: Voice links to Zoho exist, but you build them
cards.body: Automation services can hook a phone voice agent or a smart speaker up to Zoho Inventory and turn what was said into a Zoho sales order. You set up that connection and keep it working, and the caller has nothing on screen to correct.

features.h2: Not a Zoho Inventory alternative: the ordering step its portal leaves out

rows.h3: Spoken by the chef, corrected on screen, then sent
rows.body: The chef taps Push to Speak and reads off what the kitchen is short on. The app sets it out as items from that restaurant's own guide; the chef fixes any that are wrong, then sends the order. There is no store to browse and no call to your office.

cards.h2: Where Zoho Inventory's job ends and the app's begins
cards.lead: Nothing here is an alternative to Zoho Inventory. Stock, billing and the portal are still Zoho's to run; the app handles the single step none of those do, a kitchen sending its order.

items.h3: Zoho Inventory keeps the records it holds today
items.body: Your customer records, stock, batch history and invoices live there. What we hold is every kitchen's order guide with its prices, kept current by you, along with the orders kitchens place in our app.

items.h3: The portal carries on for invoices and payments
items.body: Restaurants keep looking up orders and paying bills there, as they do now. The app is only where an order starts. A call to your office still gets no number from us; only app orders get one.

items.h3: A Zoho Commerce store can stay for accounts that browse
items.body: If you run one, keep it: some accounts like to search a catalog and type. The app is for the chef who finds it quicker to talk than to search.

midcta.h3: Watch the step Zoho's portal skips: a chef's order sent from the app
midcta.body: Over a 20-minute demo, we read an order aloud into the app, edit one item on screen, and send it. Then we show the formats your desk could get it in, and what an API order would need on the Zoho side.

steps.lead: It starts with a file you already have. We build the guides from it, and each restaurant can begin ordering in the app.

items.body: The price list or item export Zoho already produces, saved as Excel or CSV, is usually all we need.

items.h3: Orders land in the format you picked

comparison.h2: Zoho Inventory plus VoiceOrder Solutions. Your stock and portal stay put.
h2_lines: Your stock and portal stay put.
comparison.lead: Your warehouses, batch records and billing stay in Zoho whichever way you go. If a Zoho Inventory alternative is what you searched for, the real gap is narrower: the portal Zoho gives your customers is built for viewing and paying invoices, with no ordering inside it. There is no built-in tie between the two products, and each is bought separately.

faq.h2: Questions from teams that run Zoho Inventory

items.q: Do we need a Zoho Inventory alternative before kitchens can order on their own?
items.a: No. Your stock stays in Zoho, and its portal keeps handling bills and payments. The one thing the portal will not do is accept an order from the restaurant. Our app fills that gap: a chef tells it what is short, checks the items and sends them.

items.q: Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than Zoho Inventory?
items.a: For one job, yes: the order Zoho's portal cannot take, sent by a chef who would otherwise call, with every item checked first. We do not set out to be a Zoho Inventory replacement. Zoho Inventory does far more, from batches and warehouses to invoices, so the app goes beside it, not in its place.

items.q: Our kitchens already use the Zoho customer portal. Why not order there?
items.a: Because Zoho built the portal for looking things up: its help pages list viewing sales orders, paying invoices and checking deliveries, and say customers cannot order there. Zoho's answer for online ordering is a separate product, Zoho Commerce. Keep the portal either way; the app only adds the order.

items.q: Does someone here still have to enter app orders into Zoho Inventory?
items.a: It depends on the format. Zoho and VoiceOrder Solutions are separate companies, nothing ties our app to Zoho, and each supports only its own software. EDI and API orders can land in Zoho with no retyping, provided your Zoho account is able to take them in; we check that with you in the demo. When you choose email, the order is a file (PDF, Word or Excel) that the chef reviewed before sending, and someone on your side enters it from there rather than from a call or a message left overnight.

items.q: Doesn't Zoho's own AI already create orders?
items.a: Zoho's AI, Zia, answers questions about stock, orders and customers, and Zoho says AI agents can create orders through its tools. The voice links above are another route. Our app is a different thing: the chef voices the order, then checks each item from their own guide before it is sent.

items.q: Does setting this up change anything in our Zoho account?
items.a: Getting started needs no Zoho login and installs nothing: we build from a file you pull out of Zoho, and your settings and pricing are left alone. If you later want orders to arrive by EDI or the API, the demo covers what that would take on your side.

items.q: How soon can we be live, and what does it cost?
items.a: Most distributors are up and running in 24 to 48 hours. Zoho publishes its plan prices; ours is a quote for your business. Any Zoho Inventory alternative that takes over your stock means moving items, batches, warehouses and the accounting link in one go. Next to that move, adding one new way for restaurants to order is small.

items.a: From zoho.com, visited on 9 November 2026: Zoho Inventory's product, pricing, order management, AI (Zia) and mobile pages, Zoho's support articles about the portal and price lists, and Zoho Commerce's note on B2B selling.
